title: 41 AI-animated characters in a solo idle tycoon — my Veo → Godot 4 pipeline (free demo)
author: TishmanPWNZ
selftext:
I’m a solo dev making **Viral Creator**, a cozy idle tycoon about growing from a bedroom desk into a content studio (Godot 4 + C#). Every one of the 41 staff members lives in their own animated room, and getting that to look consistent took more pipeline work than I expected, so I want to share how I did it.

Each character goes through two steps. First, I give an image model two references, the character’s portrait and the room of their profession, and ask for one full-body shot of this exact character standing in this exact room. Straight image-to-video from a portrait gave me characters cut off at the knees or standing behind a desk, so this step fixes the composition before any animation happens. Then that image goes into Veo in 9:16.

Veo doesn’t give you loops, so that part is scripted. Veo often shifts the pose in the first second, so I cut the first 1.5 seconds. Then the script compares every early frame with every late frame, picks the most similar pair, and crossfades the tail back into the head. The loop has to be at least 60% of the clip; otherwise, it finds tiny jittery loops. I regenerate anything where the room drifts or the lighting flickers. For the home screen, I went further: only the window glass is taken from the Veo frames and pasted into the original room, so the room stays pixel-identical and only the city outside moves.

In-game, the team screen plays these as Theora videos. The hiring conveyor shows many cards at once, so there they become 48-frame sprite sheets at 12 fps. One fun bug: GPU texture compression works in 4×4 blocks, and until I made the cell size a multiple of 4, neighbouring frames bled into each other. Music is made with ElevenLabs on a paid plan. Code, UI, economy, and game design are mine.

I’m curious how others handle looping with video models. Is best-match plus crossfade the standard trick, or has someone found a way to get Veo (or Kling, Runway…) to produce clean loops directly?

The free demo goes up to career level 10 (Windows, EN/RU). Link in the comments, and pacing feedback is very welcome.
